title: Design System: alexboffey.co.uk

monument.purpose: The surname in the first viewport and the 404 code. Viewport-bound so it fills the measure by construction.

title.purpose: Reading-surface titles and the footer's closing line.

row-lg.purpose: CV organisation names and the practice strands.

row.purpose: Index row titles on work and writing.

lead.purpose: The positioning sentence and every standfirst. Capped at 46ch.

label.purpose: Navigation, actions, field labels. Display face, uppercase, 0.3em tracked.

extensions.shadowPhilosophy: None. There is not one box-shadow in the build. Depth comes from the lattice's atmospheric fog, tonal grounds mixed in oklab, and 1px hairlines derived from --glimmer.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Exponential ease-out, on everything.

motion.name: dur-enter
motion.purpose: The canvas fade-in once the shader is live.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All four durations collapse to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

stations.character: A skyline: tall towers, tighter grid, warm

stations.name: writing
stations.character: A plain: wide-spaced flat plates, cool

stations.name: about

stations.name: reading
stations.character: Almost empty, very flat, very far

stations.name: lost
stations.character: The lattice comes apart into shards

degradation.behaviour: The canvas never mounts. The CSS gradient ground stands in and nothing else is lost.
One frame, then stop. No loop, no travel burst, no pointer warp, no trailing cursor.
48 march steps at 0.62 render scale, versus 96 at full.
Every route renders and reads in full. The CV serves all roles open and all bullets visible.

components.name: Label
components.description: The system's connective tissue: display face, uppercase, 0.3em tracked, so small type reads as an instrument legend.

narrative.overview:
One field, seen from one angle, travelled through rather than navigated. The whole site is a full-bleed window onto a live isometric block lattice, raymarched in a single fragment shader, and the interface is a set of thin drawn marks laid over it. The projection the field holds is the projection the logo mark is already drawn in, so the field is not decoration around the identity: it is the identity, extended past the mark and into the entire page.

The register is cold, hued and industrial. Nothing here is neutral grey, nothing is neutral black, and there is exactly one warm colour in the system. Density is deliberately uneven: monumental type against hairline legends, a full viewport of atmosphere against a tight ruled list. Every surface reads as drawn rather than boxed, which is why there is not a single shadow, radius above 3px, or card anywhere in the build.

Two directions were rejected and both remain anti-references. Brutalist and Swiss poster treatments were ruled out by the client. Near-black plus a single neon accent with glowing edges was ruled out on craft grounds: it is what every engineer portfolio ships, and this ground is a genuinely hued blue-slate for exactly that reason.
keyCharacteristics: A live WebGL lattice as the persistent ground of every route
A fixed 30 degree axonometric projection, inherited from the logo mark
Exactly one accent colour, the brand orange, used sparingly enough to mean something
One variable display face driven on its width axis instead of extra weights
Hairlines and tonal grounds only: no shadows, no cards, no filled containers
The rotated square as the system's only decorative glyph
Degradation designed as a first-class behaviour, not a fallback

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: src/styles/tokens.css owns the palette for the DOM and the GPU. tokenRgb() reads --void, --echo, --glimmer, --mist, --incandescent and --ember back off the document element at mount and feeds them to the shader as vec3 uniforms. Those six tokens must stay plain six-digit hex, and no palette value may be defined anywhere but tokens.css.

rules.name: The One Hot Colour Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent and it is orange. No second accent, no semantic colour set. If a state needs marking, it is marked with the accent, with a hairline, or with opacity, never with a new hue.

rules.name: The Hued Ground Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system is neutral grey or neutral black. Every dark value carries the ground's blue-slate hue and every light value is a cooled descendant of the mark's warm grey. Mixing happens in oklab.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: When display type needs a different feel, change font-stretch, not the weight and not the family. Every display element sets an explicit width from the named scale, 72% through 92%. Never ship a second display face or an extra static weight to solve something the axis can solve.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: Small type is never just small. Anything at label or micro size is set in the display face, uppercased, and tracked to 0.3em, so it reads as an instrument legend rather than shrunken body copy.

rules.name: The Ramp Follows the Component Rule
rules.body: The row and sub-heading steps exist because the components arrived at those sizes first and the ramp was written afterwards. When a component genuinely needs a step the ramp lacks, widen the ramp and name the step. Do not leave a bare literal in a component, and do not snap a considered size to a nearby token just to satisfy a linter.

rules.name: The Local Ground Rule
rules.body: The scrim is not always enough. Five components carry their own ground because measured contrast failed over the field, and each is load-bearing rather than decorative. Do not remove these to clean up the styling, and add one when new text lands in the right half of a wide viewport. Composite the alpha against a bright cube face before trusting it: 62% was not enough and became 88%.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: If something needs to separate from what is behind it, give it a tonal ground and a hairline. Never a shadow, never a glow border, never a gradient stroke.

rules.name: The No Cards Rule
rules.body: There are no cards in this world, and this has been enforced twice against drift. If a block needs to be set apart, give it a hairline and a heading. Do not reintroduce a bordered, padded, radiused container.

rules.name: The Diamond-Only Rule
rules.body: The rotated square is the only decorative glyph. No chevrons, no arrows, no icon set, no bullets from a font. If a marker is needed, it is a diamond.

dos: Do define every palette value in src/styles/tokens.css and nowhere else, as plain six-digit hex for the six tokens the shader reads.
Do reach for font-stretch from the named width scale before a weight, and never before a second family.
Do set small type in the display face, uppercased, tracked to 0.3em.
Do give any new text in the right half of a wide viewport its own tonal ground, and composite the alpha against a bright cube face before trusting it.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px --rule hairline and a tonal ground.
Do use the rotated square when a marker is needed.
Do keep composition left-weighted, so the scrim's horizontal pass keeps working.
Do add a station when you add a route, with an unused position value.
Do make new interactive state fail open, the way the CV does: serve the readable state and let the script narrow it.
Do widen the type ramp and name the step when a component needs a size it lacks.
donts: Don't add a shadow. There are none, and depth comes from fog, tone and hairlines.
Don't add a card, a filled bordered container, or a radius above 3px.
Don't introduce a second accent or a semantic colour set. One hot colour.
Don't use a neutral grey or a neutral black anywhere outside the print palette.
Don't make the lattice camera perspective, or rotate its view direction.
Don't remove the shader's ambient floor, or raise a block dimension past FILL without redoing the step-clamp arithmetic.
Don't use a chevron, an arrow, or an icon font. The diamond is the glyph.
Don't ship a second display face or an extra static weight.
Don't leave a bare font-size or colour literal in a component.
Don't claim the shader as a hand-written work sample; it is art direction, and docs/lattice.md is its handover.

knownInconsistencies: The styling layer is mid-migration: six components on CSS Modules, EntryList, Lattice and all page-level blocks still on Astro scoped styles. Astro-specific blocker: a <script> block cannot see the hashed names, so every JS-touched class needs :global().
Local grounds have no rule distinguishing --void from --abyss. Five surfaces, five alphas, two base tokens, all arrived at by measurement.
nav__link--action is a third action treatment, against 'one shape, two weights'. Different padding, no diamond.
The webfont is 89.7 KB for two faces at full axis range across the whole latin subset, where five widths and three weights are used. Subsetting would return 40-50 KB.
No visual regression coverage. 28 Playwright tests cover behaviour, degradation and content truth, but nothing covers appearance. Snapshots need the canvas masked.
